title: FieldAnnotation
description: One box on one page of one U.S. tax form: where it is, how its value should look, and where that value lives in a taxpayer's data. This is the only object type in the spec -- a form's full annotation set is simply a JSON array of these. See README.md for the full writeup.

box_id.description: Stable, unique identifier for this exact box. Convention: <form_id>_<form_version>_<box_label>[_<disambiguator>]. Uniqueness only needs to hold within (form_id, form_version) -- the same box_id string reused under a different form_id is a different box.

label.description: Human-readable description shown to the person authoring or reviewing this annotation. Never used at render time -- purely documentation.

form_id.description: Which form this box belongs to. Lowercase, hyphenated, matching common IRS naming.

form_version.description: The tax year (or revision) this box's position/format is valid for. Forms are redesigned at least annually -- (form_id, form_version) together are this annotation's real identity. A later year's redesign is a NEW set of FieldAnnotation records, never an edit of these coordinates in place.

page.description: 1-based page number within the form. 1-based (not 0-based) because every place a human refers to this annotation -- a code review comment, a QA ticket, a support call -- says 'page 1', never 'page 0'.

data_reference.description: Where this box's value lives in the taxpayer dataset. Either a plain dot/index path, or a closed aggregate function call over a path containing a [*] wildcard. See README.md 'Data reference syntax' for the full grammar and worked examples at increasing nesting depth.

condition.description: If present, this box is only filled when the comparison holds. Absent = always fill (subject to the value existing).

Position.description: All coordinates are in POINTS (1/72 inch), always -- not a configurable per-record unit. See README.md 'Why points' for the justification. Origin is the TOP-LEFT corner of the page; x grows right, y grows down.

type.description: Drives which of the settings below apply -- see README.md's field-by-field table for the exact mapping.

decimals.description: currency / percentage. Default 2 for currency, 1 for percentage.

alignment.description: Any type. Numeric types default to right; text/date/ssn_ein_masked default to left; checkbox is ignored (always centered).

max_characters.description: text / ssn_ein_masked. A hard cap on printed character count, independent of whether the box is visually wide enough -- e.g. a database column limit upstream, not a layout constraint.

negative_style.description: currency / whole_number / percentage. Default 'parentheses', matching the IRS's own convention for negative amounts on printed forms.

date_format.description: date. A pattern using MM, DD, YYYY, YY.

mask.description: ssn_ein_masked. 'X' marks a digit slot, everything else is a literal separator. Raw digits from the data are laid into the X slots in order.

true_value.description: checkbox. The data value that counts as 'checked'. Defaults to boolean true. Setting this to something else (e.g. a specific enum string) is how several checkbox annotations sharing one data_reference model a single-select group -- see README.md 'Checkbox groups'.

Condition.description: A single comparison -- deliberately not a general boolean expression tree. See README.md 'Why not a full expression language'.

data_reference.description: The path being tested. Same grammar as the top-level data_reference, minus aggregate functions -- a condition tests one concrete value.

value.description: Comparison operand. Required for every operator except 'exists', which ignores it.
